title: Dual-Geometric Space Embedding Model for Two-View Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Two-view knowledge graphs combine an ontology view with hierarchical structure and an instance view with cyclical structure, creating heterogeneous graph structures for embedding.

gap.claim: Existing knowledge graph embedding methods generally assume a single view, or place both views in the same geometric space, which is unsuitable when different graph portions exhibit different structures.

contributions.claim: Defines and constructs a dual-geometric space embedding model that embeds different portions of a two-view knowledge graph in different geometric spaces.
Unifies spherical space, hyperbolic space, and their intersecting space for learning embeddings.
Introduces closed spherical space operators that directly use spherical-space properties without mapping to an approximate tangent space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the closed spherical space operators as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public datasets reportedly show that DGS significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art baseline models on knowledge graph completion tasks.
The authors report that the results demonstrate DGS's ability to better model heterogeneous structures in knowledge graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Two-view knowledge graphs represent ontology concepts and instantiated entities.
The two views produce hierarchical and cyclical structures, while prior embedding assumptions do not adequately represent both views.
DGS embeds different graph portions in different geometric spaces within a complex non-Euclidean framework.
The model includes closed spherical space operators that avoid approximate tangent-space mapping.
Public-dataset experiments reportedly show improved knowledge graph completion performance over prior state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: Different portions of a knowledge graph may exhibit distinct geometric structures, such as hierarchical and cyclical organization.

interpretation.claim: Embedding design can benefit from matching geometric representations to structural regimes instead of imposing one shared space.

application.claim: For heterogeneous relational data, consider decomposing the data into structural views and selecting or combining spaces suited to each view.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported knowledge graph completion setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the public datasets, baseline identities, numerical results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, optimization procedure, or computational requirements.
